qa_test_defect.root_cause: AddProcedureModal's pre-existing hardcoded default (useState<ProcedureLogKey>('botox')) is, per FE-8's own severity table (which this very test file locks in via it.each), an avoid-severity procedure for pregnancy. A pregnant profile therefore shows the pregnancy InlineAlert immediately on mount, before the test's own selectProcedure(key) call. Every failing test's pregnancyAlertCalls() helper reads the InlineAlert jest mock's cumulative call history since the last mockClear() (which runs in beforeEach, before renderModal()), so the mount-time botox call is always present alongside whatever the test's own selection produces, breaking every 'exactly N calls' assertion where the newly-selected procedure is also on-topic.
qa_test_defect.verified_with: a scratch instrumented test (InlineAlert wrapped in jest.fn, counted mock.calls.length immediately after render() with no interaction) confirmed exactly 1 call fires on mount alone for a pregnant profile with the default botox selection, before any fix; after memoizing the alert element (see deviation 4) this collapsed to exactly 1 stable call, ruling out a double-render artifact as the residual cause.
qa_test_defect.why_not_worked_around: The only implementation that would make these pass is gating the pregnancy alert on an explicit user interaction (never show it for the untouched default, even though it's genuinely selected and genuinely avoid-severity) — a real safety regression: a pregnant user who opens the modal and taps Save without touching the already-selected default would never see the warning. Declined for a safety-critical feature; left the 7 tests red instead of shipping that regression.
qa_test_defect.recommended_fix_for_qa_lead: Either call (InlineAlert as jest.Mock).mockClear() between renderModal() and selectProcedure(key) in each affected test, or assert on the LAST matching call's procedure-specific explanation text instead of raw call count.

point_a_disputed_qa_failures.verdict: QA-test defect, not an implementation gap — WARNING, not a BLOCKER
point_a_disputed_qa_failures.reasoning: Independently read tests/pregnancy-safety-handling/AddProcedureModal.pregnancy-enabled.test.tsx and src/components/clinic/AddProcedureModal.tsx, and re-ran the suite to inspect the actual failure output. Confirmed mechanically: mockClear() runs in beforeEach (before renderModal()), so the mount-time InlineAlert call for the hardcoded default 'botox' selection (avoid-severity per FE-8's own table) is never cleared before selectProcedure(key) fires a second call; toHaveLength(1) assertions see 2. The jest output's mock.calls arrays confirm exactly 2 entries (not 3), proving the useMemo double-commit fix (deviation 4) works as intended. On the merits, the underlying behavior — alerting immediately for the current selection, mount included — is the correct call, not a bug to work around: it matches the other three pre-existing checks' identical reactive-derivation-from-current-state pattern, matches spec §4 Story 3 AC1's literal Given/When ('when the user selects botox' is satisfied by botox being the currently-selected, visibly-active radio row, which it is on open), and — decisively — gating the alert on an explicit interaction would leave unwarned exactly the user most likely to matter: a pregnant user who opens the modal, accepts the pre-selected default (already correct for them), and taps Save without touching any radio row. Concur with the engineer's refusal to implement that gate. Recommend qa-lead apply fix (a) from the engineer's note (mockClear() between renderModal() and selectProcedure() in each affected test) as the correct, minimal follow-up.

point_c_planApply_gap.verdict: Confirmed real. Not a blocker for this PR — track as an explicit follow-up ticket, ideally resolved before or alongside ever flipping PREGNANCY_SAFETY_ENABLED to true.
point_c_planApply_gap.reasoning: Read planApply.ts directly: buildStepsFromPlan's clinicallyFrozen = new Set(frozen.filter((f) => f.until)...) excludes any FrozenItem without `until`, and a pregnancy freeze never sets one (confirmed in context.ts/dailyView.ts), so a previously userPinned retinoid step would survive a Draft->Save regeneration under an active pregnancy freeze. Real, but: (1) zero current exposure — PREGNANCY_SAFETY_ENABLED is false, so this whole feature including this gap is fully inert today; (2) narrow even once enabled — every other surface (new-plan eligibility, Today screen via both dailyView.ts call sites, the substitute/swap flow, validate.ts's saved-routine findings) correctly enforces the freeze; only the specific pin-before-freeze plus Draft->Save path leaks; (3) this is a pre-existing architectural gap shared with pair-rule freezes (also until-less), not a new defect pattern this task introduced; (4) planApply.ts is explicitly outside tech design §3's scope, and changing its until-based semantics is a cross-cutting call affecting the pair-rule freeze path too, correctly deferred to tech-lead/product rather than a unilateral fix.
